explain.say: China's Three Gorges Dam, the biggest power station on Earth, and a coal plant in Gujarat share the same heart: the synchronous generator. On the board, steam spins a turbine at 3000 rpm, the shaft turns a rotor that is an electromagnet, and the stator coils around it deliver three-phase power to the grid.

explain.say: Now the real thing in 3D: a power station's turbine and generator. Steam spins the blades, the coupling turns the generator rotor, and the stator windings deliver the power. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

draw.text: Synchronous generators: how a power station turns a spinning shaft into 50 hertz

explain.say: Look at the rotor. Fed with DC from the exciter, it is a spinning magnet, and its field sweeps past the stator coils, inducing an AC voltage in each. The rotor is locked in step, synchronous, with that voltage: a 2-pole rotor at 3000 rpm makes exactly 50 cycles a second. What speed would a 2-pole machine need for 60 hertz?

explain.say: 3600 rpm, as in the USA. Slow water turbines use rotors with many poles instead: 40 poles at 150 rpm also make 50 hertz. Now the exciter. Turning up its field current raises the generated voltage E, and on a big grid that mainly changes the reactive power the machine supplies, which holds up the grid voltage. So what decides the real power it sends?

explain.say: The steam valve. Open it and the rotor edges ahead of the grid by an angle called delta, the power angle. Power sent equals E times V over X, times sine delta. With E of 1.2, V of 1.0 and a reactance of 0.8 per unit, at 30 degrees it sends 0.75 per unit. Look along the curve: what happens beyond 90 degrees?

curves.label: P = 1.5 sin δ
curves.ask: What is the power angle of a generator?

explain.say: Beyond 90 degrees more angle gives less power, so the rotor would race ahead and slip out of step, a loss of synchronism that protection must catch fast. That is why operators keep delta well below 90 degrees. Superb! Challenge: how much power does this generator send at 60 degrees?

Real machines run well below 90° to keep a safety margin

faq.q: How does a power station generator make 50 Hz?
faq.a: A turbine spins the rotor, a DC electromagnet, at a fixed speed. Frequency equals poles times rpm over 120, so a 2-pole rotor at 3000 rpm gives exactly 50 hertz.
asks: Why do generators spin at 3000 rpm?

faq.q: What does excitation do in a synchronous generator?
faq.a: Excitation is the DC current in the rotor winding that makes its magnetic field. More excitation raises the internal voltage, which on a grid mainly increases the reactive power the generator supplies and supports the voltage.

faq.q: What is the power angle of a generator?
faq.a: It is the angle by which the rotor's internal voltage leads the grid voltage. Real power sent is E V over X times sine delta, so more turbine power pushes delta larger.
asks: What is the load angle delta?

faq.a: If the turbine pushes more power than E V over X can carry, or a fault upsets the balance, delta passes the stable limit and the rotor slips poles relative to the grid. Protection then trips the unit to avoid damage.

faq.q: Why do hydro generators have so many poles?
faq.a: Water turbines turn slowly, perhaps 100 to 300 rpm. To make 50 hertz at low speed the rotor needs many poles: 40 poles at 150 rpm gives 40 times 150 over 120, which is 50 hertz.
asks: Why are hydro generators so wide?

facts: The Three Gorges Dam in China is the world's largest power station, at about 22.5 GW.
Generator frequency f = pn/120: 2 poles at 3000 rpm or 4 poles at 1500 rpm give 50 Hz.
Large turbo-generators in coal and nuclear plants usually have 2 or 4 poles.

quiz.say: A generator has E of 1.2, V of 1.0 and X of 0.8 per unit. What power does it send at a power angle of 60 degrees?
quiz.show: A generator has E = 1.2 pu, V = 1.0 pu, X = 0.8 pu. What power does it send at δ = 60°?
quiz.why: P equals 1.2 times 1.0 over 0.8, which is 1.5, times sine 60 degrees, 0.866: about 1.30 per unit.

wrong.1: 0.75 per unit is the power at 30 degrees.
wrong.2: 1.5 per unit is the maximum, reached only at 90 degrees.

quiz.say: How many poles does a 50 hertz hydro generator need at 150 rpm?
quiz.show: How many poles does a 50 Hz hydro generator need at 150 rpm?
quiz.why: Poles equal 120 times frequency over speed: 120 times 50 over 150 is 40.

wrong.1: 20 poles at 150 rpm would give only 25 hertz.
wrong.2: 4 poles would need 1500 rpm for 50 hertz.
